title: Adaptive queue-shedding and preemptive scaling after hosted GPU backlog spike
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Post-incident follow-up for the hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event on 2025-02-11 where queue growth caused large tail latencies and aggressive throttling. This ticket drives work to implement an adaptive queue shedding policy, preemptive scale-up triggers, and improved telemetry to avoid recurrence and reduce customer-visible 5xx/429 spikes.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-11 03:10-04:05 UTC, the hosted API experienced sustained GPU pool saturation in us-west-2 leading to a queue backlog that exceeded soft queue thresholds. The autoscaler reacted slowly because the observed metric window used p95 token time which lagged by ~90s. As backlog grew, the service began shedding requests inconsistently (mix of 429s and 503s) and customers observed elevated latencies and error rates for ~55 minutes. No data exfiltration or security exposure occurred.
timeline:
- 03:05 UTC: Traffic surge from a customer batch job + multiple tenants with long-context generation requests.
- 03:10 UTC: GPU utilization p95 crossed 95% in primary pool; queue length began increasing rapidly.
- 03:18 UTC: Autoscaler triggered scale but provisioning delayed due to capacity fragmentation and instance boot time (~4 minutes).
- 03:25 UTC: Queue > 120s tail latency; runtime started opportunistic shedding; some requests received 429, some were retried and became 503 due to timeouts.
- 04:05 UTC: Manual mitigation: routing a portion of traffic to cold spare pool and increasing limit for dedicated pool; queue drained by 04:15 UTC.
root_cause: 1) Autoscaler relied on a smoothed p95 token time that delayed reaction to sharp queue growth; 2) No early shedding policy for long-running low-throughput requests, allowing a small number of large jobs to monopolize burstable slots and KV cache entries; 3) Inconsistent shedding logic between gateway and runtime produced mixed 429/503 semantics, confusing clients and retry logic.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Implement adaptive queue-shedding (early drops) for requests that exceed expected token-per-second profile at the gateway to reduce tail impact. Tradeoff: increases client-visible 429s but limits 503s and system-wide latency.
- Introduce a fast-path preemptive scale trigger using short-window queue growth (>30s growth) and hot-slot pressure. Tradeoff: may provision extra capacity more often during noisy spikes; mitigated by cooldown and fractional scale steps.
- Standardize the client-facing error code to prefer 429 for rate-limited drops and surface retry-after headers. Tradeoff: some clients will need to adjust backoff logic; long-term this is clearer and easier to handle in SDKs.
action_items: A1: Implement gateway-level adaptive queue shedder that evaluates request cost signature (expected tokens, model class, context length) and drops low-value long-running requests when queue growth > threshold. Owner: Carlos Mendes. Estimate: 5 pts. Due: 2025-03-03
A2: Add a short-window (10s) queue-velocity metric and hook it into autoscaler to allow fractional preemptive scale steps. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2025-02-27

A3: Normalize error semantics: gateway returns 429 with Retry-After for shed requests; runtime returns 503 only for internal failures. Update SDKs and docs. Owner: Evan Liu. Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2025-03-10

A4: Create a canary in us-west-2 that runs the new shedder + short-window autoscaler for 48h with synthetic traffic and 3 customer workloads. Owner: SRE Team (lead: Marta Kovacs). Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2025-03-12

A5: Instrument new telemetry: queue-velocity, per-model long-request ratio, shed-rate by tenant, and Retry-After usage. Add dashboard and automated alert when shed-rate > 0.5% for 10m. Owner: Observability (lead: Samir Patel). Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2025-02-28
A6: Capacity hygiene: define and run a weekly prewarm job for cold spare pools and improve fragmentation packing heuristics. Owner: Infra (lead: Anita Gomez). Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2025-03-20
success_criteria:
- Median and p95 tail latency reductions during spikes: p95 token latency <= pre-incident baseline + 20%.
- Shed-rate limited to <1% during normal traffic and <5% during spikes with clear Retry-After headers.
- No more than one customer-visible 5xx surge per quarter attributed to queue backlog.
- Alerts trigger and paging occurs before customer-visible latencies increase (queue-velocity detects growth > 30s).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Premature shedding may break legitimate long-generations for paying customers. Mitigation: Use per-tenant SLA exemptions and gradual rollout (canary + opt-out list).
- Risk: Autoscaler false positives on synthetic spikes. Mitigation: require both queue-velocity and hot-slot pressure before scaling.
- Risk: SDKs not honoring Retry-After leading to thundering retries. Mitigation: ship SDK change simultaneously and add client metrics to detect non-compliant clients.

2025-02-15 Priya Nair: Autoscaler PoC uses queue-velocity metric — initial tests show scale reaction time reduced from ~90s to ~18s in lab.
2025-02-18 Marta Kovacs: SRE will prepare canary harness. Need a short list of 3 customer tenants that can opt into early testing.
